newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour MP faces punishment over sleaze.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour MP faces punishment over sleaze.

text.p: A member of Britain's ruling Labour party was facing a one-week suspension from parliament on Tuesday in the first case of sleaze since Prime Minister Tony Blair swept to power three months ago.

Parliament's powerful Committee on Standards and Privileges recommended that Labour member of parliament Robert Wareing make an apology to the House of Commons and then be suspended for making a false declaration about his business interests.
"We find Mr Wareing's conduct wrong," the committee said.
The last MPs to be temporarily suspended were two Conservatives who took cash in return for agreeing to ask questions in parliament.

Labour acted swiftly to limit the damage after allegations were made in June that Wareing had failed to declare an interest in a company, of which he was the sole director, that received a 6,000 pound retainer in 1994 from a firm believed to be a front organisation for the Bosnian Serb government.
Pending parliament's inquiry, Labour suspended Wareing from its parliamentary party and from representing Labour in any official capacity.
A Labour spokesman said these sanctions would remain in force until the party reviewed Tuesday's findings. This would probably not be before November.
The all-party Standards and Privileges Committee said it agreed with parliament's ethics commissioner, Sir Gordon Downey, that Wareing should have registered his directorship.
But Downey said in a report to the panel that he saw no evidence that Wareing was trying to avoid tax or that the retainer was paid by a front for the Bosnian Serbs.

"I have discussed these findings with Mr Wareing who agrees with the facts and the balance of presentation. He accepts that his interest should have been registered but asks the Committee to accept that failure to do so was due to oversight and not an attempt at concealment," Downey wrote.
